title: why a file note's extra anchors can never carry symbols
summary: A file note can accumulate anchors it is structurally incapable of ever filling: every path listed in a write's `verified` becomes an anchor, but only ONE of them — the anchor whose path derives the note id — is addressable by a later write. kbWrite routes a file note by spec.path and overwrites the record's anchors with a single entry at that path, so there is no spec that attaches symbols to a secondary anchor; a write aimed at one lands on whatever note that path derives to instead. Any code that walks a note's anchors and tries to fill them one by one is therefore writing to the wrong note and never converging, which is exactly how the keeper's auto-backfill disabled itself. Observed live 2026-08-03: a note written with verified:[src/alpha.ts, src/beta.ts] gained two anchors, and only the alpha one could ever be given symbols.
identityAliases: one addressable anchor per file note

steps.role: routes a file note by spec.path (fileNoteId) and overwrites record.anchors with one entry at that path — the constraint everything else inherits
stamps an anchor for every path in `verified`, which is how secondary anchors appear at all (observed via behaviour this session, file not read)
the consumer that must respect it — fills only the anchor whose path derives the note id, skipping the rest

invariants: exactly one anchor per file note is addressable by a write: the one where fileNoteId(anchor.path) === note.id
a fill loop over note.anchors must skip every other anchor or it writes to a different note and re-fires forever
